citation: Kaslow, Cahill, and Frank (2019), Developing a CubeSat System MBSE Reference Model – Interim Status #5
title: Developing a CubeSat System MBSE Reference Model – Interim Status #5
venue_type: conference paper; venue name not stated in paper.md
modeling_scope: SysML CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) for a CubeSat space-and-ground system. Scope covers requirements and architecture hierarchies from domain/enterprise to segments, subsystems, and components, including the Power Subsystem/Power Components; stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, model population, CSRM-to-MSM application, logical-to-physical architecture transition, and general validation/verification activities. The CSRM is a reusable, tailorable reference model rather than a mission-specific populated model.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML using an unspecified graphical modeling tool; CSRM/MSM reference-model workflow with Foundational CSRM, Web Published CSRM, and CSRM XMI File. No specific vendor tool is named.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite platform; paper describes CubeSat as 1U with larger 3U, 6U, and 12U form factors, and addresses mission-specific CubeSat space and ground systems. No named mission is reported.
task_domain: CubeSat mission and system design/development, including space segment, ground segment, mission-specific logical and physical architectures, and university-level CubeSat design/build use.
interface: Model/tool interface includes CSRM delivery as Foundational CSRM, Web Published CSRM, and CSRM XMI File for mission teams to load into a graphical modeling tool. Engineering interfaces include CubeSat Deployer Systems stakeholders/deployer interface requirements and component interfaces, power, weight, cost, and performance properties.
feedback: General assessment loops are described: verification activities provide data for the technical measurement process; CSRM validation is to use RFP requirement satisfaction, SysML model-evaluation questions, and evaluations by mission-specific CubeSat teams. No closed-loop simulation feedback is reported.
evaluation: The paper demonstrates the CSRM through SysML package/diagram excerpts and defines validation approaches for the CSRM/MSM: OMG RFP requirement satisfaction, Practical Guide to SysML model-evaluation questions, and evaluation by mission-specific CubeSat teams/trusted partners. It states the model is mature enough for validation, but does not report completed empirical validation results.
rq_relevance: RQ1 yes: the paper presents a general, reusable CubeSat system MBSE reference model in SysML, including a power subsystem/components within the architecture hierarchy, but it is not an EPS-specific behavior model. RQ2 partial: it claims reuse, sharing, integration/traceability, and a central design baseline from model use, but does not claim EPS-specific reliability outcomes. RQ3 partial: it explicitly models general verification and validation activities, plans, procedures, results, status, and verify/validate relationships, but the V&V linkage is system-level rather than EPS-specific.
claimed_outcomes: CSRM logical components are intended to be reused as a starting point for mission-specific CubeSat logical and physical architecture development.
Using the CSRM for a mission-specific CubeSat is claimed to establish a mechanism to share and reuse components with other design activities.

The model is claimed to integrate stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, requirements, architecture, and validation/verification relationships through package diagrams, tables, and element properties.
The Mission-specific CubeSat Model (MSM) is claimed to serve as the single central design baseline throughout development and operations.

Requirements satisfaction can be recorded in model tables with links to CSRM elements/packages and exported for external review. Reliability improvement is not reported. EPS-specific reproducibility/integrability outcomes are not separately claimed.
verification_validation_linkage: General MSM V&V is explicitly modeled. Verification Activity elements verify requirements through verify/verifies/verified-by relationships and may capture verification plans, procedures, execution/conduct, results, and status in element properties, activity diagrams, or Word documents. Validation Activity elements validate technical measures or mission objectives through validates/validated-by relationships and analogous plan/procedure/result/status fields. This is not presented as EPS-specific verification, although the architecture includes a Power Subsystem/Power Components.
key_findings: The CSRM is an INCOSE SSWG CubeSat system reference model and proposed OMG normative specification using SysML for a space-and-ground CubeSat system.

The CSRM provides a reusable logical architecture and requirements hierarchy that mission teams tailor into a Mission-specific CubeSat Model (MSM), then into mission-specific logical and physical architectures.

The architecture hierarchy includes CubeSat bus subsystems and components, including a Power Subsystem/Power Components, but detailed EPS behavior or power parametrics are not developed in this paper.

Mission teams are expected to populate stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, requirements, selected artifacts, component interfaces, and component properties such as power, weight, cost, and performance.

The model includes explicit verification and validation element types and relationships for linking requirements, technical measures, mission objectives, and activities with plans/procedures/results/status.
CSRM validation is framed as future/ongoing: satisfaction of OMG RFP requirements, model-evaluation criteria from A Practical Guide to SysML, and evaluation by mission-specific CubeSat teams.
limitations_gaps: The CSRM is not pre-populated with specific stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, or requirements; mission-specific teams must populate and tailor these elements.
The paper states that abstraction levels for requirements, constraints, and logical design are suggestions and must be tailored to mission purpose.
The paper identifies a trade-off between insufficient detail and unnecessary detail in requirements development/truncation.
Parametrics for power, weight, and cost have not been added because the authors judge them more appropriate for a physical model.
CSRM validation appears not yet completed: initial satisfaction is based on the CSRM development team's judgment and is said to be best evaluated by mission-specific CubeSat teams.

quality.rationale: The document is a conference-style paper, but the venue name is not stated in paper.md. It discusses practical gaps and pending validation/tailoring issues, but not as a formal limitations or threats-to-validity section.

evidence_quotes.quote: The International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) Space Systems Working Group (SSWG) has been investigating the applicability of MBSE for designing CubeSats including developing a CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM). Our application of MBSE is enabled by the graphical modeling language Systems Modeling Language (SysML).

evidence_quotes.claim: Reference model intended for mission-specific CubeSat design/build and OMG specification
evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM is intended for use at the university level for designing and building a mission-specific CubeSat. Additionally, the CSRM will be submitted to the Object Management Group (OMG) as a candidate OMG Specification.

evidence_quotes.claim: System-level scope across space and ground systems
evidence_quotes.quote: The name has been changed from CubeSat Reference Model (CRM) to CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) to reflect that this model encompasses the space and ground systems not just the CubeSat itself.

evidence_quotes.claim: Reusable logical architecture for mission-specific models
evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM provides the logical architecture of a CubeSat space and ground system. The CSRM logical components are intended to be reused as a starting point for a mission-specific CubeSat logical architecture followed by the development of physical architecture during CubeSat development.

evidence_quotes.claim: Reference model is not pre-populated and supports reuse/sharing
evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM is a repository for systems engineering artifacts. However, it is not pre-populated with specific stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, and requirements. That is the job of the mission-specific CubeSat team. Development of a mission-specific CubeSat utilizing the CSRM establishes a mechanism to share and reuse components with other design activities.
the levels of abstraction in the CSRM for requirements, constraints and logical design are presented as suggestions and must be tailored to the mission purpose.
Our application of MBSE is demonstrated using Systems Modeling Language (SysML) and a graphical modeling tool.

evidence_quotes.claim: Power/EPS appears as part of component and property modeling
evidence_quotes.quote: Populate component properties such as power, weight, cost, and performance - which can be rolled up from components to subsystems to the CubeSat
evidence_quotes.location: Transition: MSM Logical Architecture MSM Physical Architecture

evidence_quotes.quote: The MSM is maintained throughout all phases of development and operations as the single and central design baseline.

The Verification Activity element describes the process for verifying an element, e.g. a requirement. For example, the process could include verification plans, procedures, execution, results, and status.

evidence_quotes.claim: Verify relationship links requirements and test/model elements
evidence_quotes.quote: The verify relationship is a relationship between a requirement and a test case or other model element that is used to verify the requirement is satisfied.

The Validation Activity element describes the process for validating an element, e.g. a Technical Measure or a Mission Objective. For example, the process could include validation plans, procedures, execution, results, and status.
Verification activities provide data to the technical measurement process that is used to assess how well the technical measure is either projected to meet, or is meeting, its stated value.

evidence_quotes.claim: CSRM validation evidence planned through mission team evaluation
evidence_quotes.quote: Initially satisfaction of these validation requirements is based on the judgment of the CSRM development team. However, the satisfaction of these validation requirements is best evaluated by several Mission-specific CubeSat teams as noted in Figure 20.
The Next Steps section of Reference [5] mentioned adding parametrics for power, weight, and cost. They have not been added since they are more appropriate for a physical model.

notes_for_consistency: Read only paper.md. No DOI or venue name is reported in the paper text. This paper is part of an interim CSRM lineage and cites Interim Status #4 plus related technical-measure and behavior papers. Treat as system-level CubeSat MBSE evidence: EPS/power is present only as Power Subsystem/Power Components and power-related component properties, not as a detailed EPS behavior or verification model. V&V is general MSM/CSRM V&V, not EPS-specific.
